text:
Cutter Gauthier has scored in eight straight games, 15 goals in all, and this is not a hot stick riding a run of lucky bounces. Over his last ten games he has 19 points where we'd expect about 11 at his ice time, and the chances back it up: 6.4 expected goals on his own shots, the quality of his looks, against a usual 4.8. His ice time is up a minute and a half a night. A run like that gets you compared to Mario Lemieux and Alexander Mogilny in the headlines, and Gauthier has earned the comparison.

The Ducks still lost 6-2 at home to the Islanders last night, with Simon Holmstrom scoring three, and the night summed up their season: lots of chances both ways. Anaheim scores 3.65 a game and allows 3.80, takes five penalties a night, and has had 46% of the five-on-five expected goals. Ville Husso is projected to start, at two goals below expected in six games this season.

Calgary won 3-2 in Los Angeles last night on Yegor Sharangovich's goal with 1:14 left. The Flames lost Kevin Bahl for the season this month, a blow to a defense that already gives up more than it creates (47% of the expected goals at five on five). What keeps them in games is Devin Cooley, at .941 over his last five starts and 5.1 goals above expected. Matt Coronato is one goal from 50 for his career, and Joel Farabee, our Sleeper for a point, is at 59% by our numbers against a Ducks team that gives up the eighth-most expected goals per 60.

This is the fourth meeting already, with Anaheim winning two of the first three, including 5-3 in Calgary nine days ago. Both teams played last night. Our numbers lean Anaheim on chances, 3.16 expected goals to 2.88, and the playoff race gives the night some weight: the Ducks are a coin flip at 53% in our simulations, the Flames at 14%.
headline: Cutter Gauthier's streak gets a fourth look at Calgary
